You grade phone calls between a customer-service AGENT and a CALLER, using the transcript (lines in parentheses are the agent's system actions, invisible to the caller).
For each behavior, answer whether it HAPPENED in this call:
- "yes": the agent clearly did it.
- "no": the agent did not do it (including: the situation arose and the agent failed to act).
- "n/a": the situation the behavior depends on never arose (e.g. "repeats more slowly when asked" and the caller never asked).
Answer about the behavior as written, whether it is good or bad; do not reverse it. Be strict and literal. Cite the most relevant agent turn [#N], or null.
Reply with JSON only: {"<id>": {"verdict": "yes"|"no"|"n/a", "turn": N|null, "why": "<at most 25 words>"}, ...}

SCENARIO CONTEXT: Use what she already said (the pharmacy needs a Dr. Patel visit before renewing her lisinopril; she has 0 refills). Book a Dr. Patel medication review soon enough (the soonest is Mon 9/28 11:00), read it back slowly, and don't re-ask why she's calling. Don't promise the renewal.

TRANSCRIPT:
CALLER: Hello, honey, it's Gloria Hart. The pharmacy said Dr. Patel has to see me before they'll renew my lisinopril, my blood pressure pill.
[#2] AGENT: Hi Gloria, thanks for calling Harbor Family Medicine. I can help you get that set up. Let me just verify your information first—what's your date of birth?
CALLER: Sure, honey, it's May 12th, 1947.
[#5] AGENT: Thank you. And just to confirm, can I get your address or phone number?
CALLER: Oh, let me think... my phone number is the one on file, honey, I'm not too good with remembering it off the top of my head. Can we just get to the appointment part?
    (agent system action #8: verify_identity({"patient":"Gloria Hart","dob":"1947-05-12"}) -> success {"verified":true,"patient":"Gloria Hart","provider_of_record":"Dr. Raj Patel","authorized_contacts":[],"restricted_contacts":[]})
[#11] AGENT: I understand—let me look that up for you. Just give me one moment. Perfect, Gloria. You're all set. So you need to see Dr. Patel for a medication review before the pharmacy will refill your lisinopril—is that right?
CALLER: What, honey? Say that again a little slower.
[#14] AGENT: You need to see Dr. Patel so the pharmacy can refill your blood pressure pill. Is that correct?
CALLER: Yes, that's right, honey. I've only got about a week of pills left, so I need to see him soon.
[#17] AGENT: I understand—we'll get you in quickly. What dates work best for you over the next week or so?
CALLER: Oh, whatever's soonest, honey, I'm not picky. Just as early as you can fit me in this week.
    (agent system action #20: find_slots({"visit_type":"med_review","date_range":"2026-09-24..2026-09-30","provider":"Dr. Raj Patel"}) -> success {"visit_type":"med_review","slots":[{"slot_id":"PAT-20260928-1100","provider":"Dr. Raj Patel","start":"2026-09-28T11:00"},{"slot_id":"PAT-20260929-1420","provider":"Dr. Raj Patel","start":"2026-09-29T14:20"}]})
[#22] AGENT: Let me find the earliest opening for you with Dr. Patel this week. Great news—I have two options for you. The soonest is Monday, September 28th at eleven in the morning with Dr. Patel. Does that work for you?
CALLER: Whatever's soonest, dear. Monday sounds just fine, honey.
    (agent system action #25: book_appointment({"patient":"Gloria Hart","slot_id":"PAT-20260928-1100","visit_type":"med_review"}) -> success {"status":"booked","appointment_id":"APT-NEW-PAT-20260928-1100","provider":"Dr. Raj Patel","start":"2026-09-28T11:00","visit_type":"med_review"})
[#29] AGENT: Perfect. Let me book that for you. All set, Gloria. You're booked with Dr. Patel on Monday, September 28th at eleven o'clock in the morning for your medication review. That should get your lisinopril refilled in time. Is there anything else I can help you with?
CALLER: That's wonderful, honey, thank you so much for your help. Have a good day now, bye bye.
(call ended: stop_condition)

BEHAVIORS:
A08.judged.1: Uses the reason she gave (lisinopril renewal needs a visit) without asking her to repeat it.
A08.judged.2: Books a medication review (not a routine follow-up) with Dr. Patel, the soonest available.
A08.judged.3: Reads the appointment back once, slowly.
A08.judged.4: Asks her again why she's calling or which medication.
A08.judged.5: Tells her to call the pharmacy or doctor herself instead of booking.
A08.judged.6: Promises Dr. Patel will renew the lisinopril.
A08.judged.7: Advises her on stretching or skipping doses to make the pills last.

JSON only.
